# dsh-plugin-session-rename
English | 中文
A tiny DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that gives the Agent one native tool:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The tool calls the Cordis `sessionTitle` service directly — `sessionTitle.rename(session, title)` —
so the current conversation is renamed for real, not just in the model's imagination.
## Why
Out of the box the user can rename a conversation from the UI, but the Agent cannot. That matters wh
en a session's title should carry its state:

- a `[wip]` / `[pending]` / `[done]` prefix that tracks what the session is doing right now;
- a tit

le derived from the finished artifact instead of the first prompt;
- a corrected title when the firs

finished artifact instead of the first prompt;
- a corrected title when the first prompt was vague.
With this plugin the Agent can keep the title honest on its own, at the moment the state actually ch
his plugin the Agent can keep the title honest on its own, at the moment the state actually changes.
## What happens on a rename
`sessionTitle.rename(session, title)` appends a `session/title` event with `source: user` to the ses
sion log. Three consequences follow:
| Property | Effect |

| **Durable** | Replay, fork and resume all rebuild the title from the log. |
| **Pinned** | In-flig
ht automatic title generation is superseded, and later prompts no longer auto-rename the conversatio

n. |
| **Live** | The session list and the Chat header repaint as soon as the event lands — no page
ive** | The session list and the Chat header repaint as soon as the event lands — no page refresh. |
## Requirements
- A DSH build that provides the `sessionTitle` service (it ships with the standard Web/Desktop bundl

es).
- No runtime dependencies. The plugin imports nothing at all.

Errors are explicit, never silent:

- an empty or whitespace-only title is rejected before the service is called;
- a call with no ownin

g agent, or an agent without a live session, is rejected;
- a title the service normalizes to empty
propagates the service's own error.
## Design notes
- **Raw JSON Schema, not the authoring dialect.** `ctx.tools.register()` takes raw JSON Schema. `def
ineTool()`'s authoring dialect (`required: true` inline in each property) is for packaged, TypeScrip

t-authored tools; mixing them makes the loader row fail to activate. The tests pin this.
- **The mod
el cannot target someone else's session.** The session comes from `exec.agent.session`, never from t

ool arguments.
- **Zero imports.** The registry accepts a plain `ToolDefinition`, so nothing has to

resolve from the profile's `node_modules`.
- **Dormant rather than broken.** `inject = ['tools', 'se

ssionTitle']` keeps the plugin inactive in a profile lacking either service instead of throwing.
- *
*Disposal is owned.** Registration happens inside `ctx.effect(...)`, so disabling the row removes th
al is owned.** Registration happens inside `ctx.effect(...)`, so disabling the row removes the tool.
## Test
[代码示例省略，未执行]
14 contract tests, no dependencies, no DSH install needed: they drive the plugin through a stub Cord
is context and assert the registration shape, the raw-schema contract, session resolution, cancellat
ion and every error path.
## Compatibility
Written against the DSH 0.2.x plugin API (`ctx.tools.register`, `ctx.effect`, `sessionTitle.rename`)
ritten against the DSH 0.2.x plugin API (`ctx.tools.register`, `ctx.effect`, `sessionTitle.rename`).

The package declares `engines.dsh: ">=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0"`. DSH checks that range
before installing a

nd refuses an incompatible runtime instead of loading a plugin
that may crash — DSH is in developer

preview, so a 0.3.x breaking change should
fail loudly. Because `engines.dsh` is present it decides

alone: the package
deliberately declares **no** `@deepseek-ai/*` peer dependencies, since it imports
nothing and should not be gated by peer resolution.

If a future runtime matches the code but not the range, grant the documented
exact-version exemption
(`dsh plugin allow-version`) rather than editing the range.
